2. Defense Sites
Of all the land and water use areas affected by the proposed Treaty, the U.S. defense sites* will involve the fewest changes. Public access to them will continue to be restricted. Construction required by relocation of military activites will be in areas of existing structures and will be quite limited so that no changes are anticipated that will have significant environmental impacts. Because planning on this has just started, it is impossible at this stage to assess these impacts in detail. Military housing areas will continue to be held and maintained by DOD as long as they are necessary. As and if military housing becomes surplus, it will be turned over to Panama.
Restriction on access to these defense sites will have a favorable impact on environmental protection in these areas, which include sites of interest to scientists and ecologists such as Fort Sherman and Galeta Island.
* Ft. Kobbe-Howard, Rodman Navy Station, Ft. Sherman, Galeta Island, Ft. Davis, Semaphore Hill, Ft. Clayton and Corozal, Albrook West as well as military hospitals and schools.
